label: Любимый
description: A 10-sentence card for любимый, the present passive participle of любить.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative. Любимый comes from любить — the second-conjugation form любим plus -ый. It agrees with masculine singular учитель and has lexicalized into the adjective beloved or favourite.

Strategic focus: Feminine nominative. The feminine ending -ая lets любимая agree with песня. As a present passive participle it literally means the one being loved, but here it simply means favourite song.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative. Любимое carries the neuter ending -ое to match блюдо. The -им- suffix marks the second conjugation, and the word names the dish that is loved.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative. The plural ending -ые lets любимые agree with книги. The participle declines like an ordinary adjective and means the beloved books.

Strategic focus: Masculine accusative. With the inanimate masculine object роман the participle keeps the form любимый as the novel I reread. Любимый роман equals роман, который любят — the novel that people love.

Strategic focus: Feminine genitive. Любимой takes the feminine genitive ending to agree with книги, marking the book that is loved as the source. The -им- suffix comes from the second-conjugation любим.
Strategic focus: Masculine dative. The dative noun гостю pulls любимому into the dative -ому ending. The word names the cherished guest and behaves wholly like an adjective.
Strategic focus: Neuter instrumental. After гордится the noun делом stands in the instrumental, and любимым takes the matching neuter instrumental ending to agree with the work she loves.
Strategic focus: Masculine prepositional. The preposition о governs the prepositional case, so городе and любимом both take prepositional endings and agree as the beloved city we discuss.

Strategic focus: Plural lexicalization. Любимые here is fully an adjective meaning favourite, formed from любим with -ые. It agrees with plural актёры and shows how the passive participle settled into everyday speech.
